story.title: More reward signals can teach the wrong behavior
paragraphs: A final correct-or-incorrect reward is clear but sparse. Checks for formatting, intermediate progress or reasoning steps add feedback, but they also change what the policy is rewarded for, so the design problem is how to combine them.

In math training on GSM8K and MATH together, adding a format reward to the outcome reward raises GSM8K accuracy from 82.6% to 86.4% but lowers MATH from 58.8% to 55.9%. Averaging all primitives has the same trade-off (86.5% and 55.8%).

mechanism.title: Judge a reward by the policy it teaches
paragraphs: DERL makes reward design the action space of a second model. This Meta-Optimizer proposes a symbolic expression over supplied atomic primitives; an inner policy is trained with that reward, and its held-out performance becomes the Meta-Optimizer’s reward. GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) trains both levels: the policy on the generated reward, the generator on the policy’s validation performance.

In the agent setup, step rewards [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0] over six steps give three stage primitives (0.5, 1 and 0, the averages of each third) plus the final success signal. Multiplying the three, for instance, would erase the early progress because the last stage scores zero; averaging would keep partial credit.

Standard DERL restarts the inner policy from the base model for each candidate reward, so validation differences reflect the reward. DERL-pop continues from the previous round’s best policy with the same total inner-loop steps, letting the reward adapt as the learner improves; the paper attributes DERL-pop’s higher scores to this curriculum-like effect. Format-valid SFT examples, constrained decoding and penalties for invalid expressions keep proposals executable.

evidence.title: Generalization requires more than dense feedback
paragraphs: On ALFWorld, averaging the primitives helps on the familiar L0 split but barely changes the held-out-task L2 split, where DERL leads by a wide margin: denser feedback alone does not transfer. In math, DERL reaches 87.0% on GSM8K and 60.2% on MATH, avoiding the format reward’s trade-off.
“Differentiable” refers to the outer update, a policy-gradient estimate over generated reward programs; nothing is backpropagated through task correctness or through the inner training runs.

demo.title: What the Meta-Optimizer proposed, and what each proposal taught
demo.caption: At each outer step the Meta-Optimizer samples eight reward expressions over four primitives; each trains a policy, and the policies’ validation scores, compared within the group, train the Meta-Optimizer. Play runs the four printed steps stage by stage. Edit the trajectory to see what every expression pays a success and a failure.
